examples.en: Our team won big in the final.
Yesterday's game ended in a landslide win for us.
Fans cheered at the news of the big win.
This election was a landslide victory for the ruling party.
A big win looked certain, but they were caught up at the end.

examples.ko: 이렇게 큰 점수 차는 대승이라고 부를 만해요.
examples.en: A score gap this big can be called a landslide.

explain: 점수 차나 결과가 크게 이겼을 때 쓰고, '대승을 거두다'가 가장 자주 나오는 말이에요. 반대로 크게 졌을 때는 '대패'라고 해요. 스포츠나 선거 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when a win is by a wide margin, and '대승을 거두다' is the most common pattern. When a team loses badly, the word is '대패'. It appears often in sports and election news.

examples.en: I fully enjoyed my freedom in Jeju over the weekend.

examples.ko: 아이들은 눈 덮인 산에서 겨울을 만끽하고 있어요.
examples.en: The kids are soaking up winter on the snow-covered mountain.
I turned off my phone to fully enjoy my first vacation in a long time.
Feel the sea breeze and savor the leisure.

examples.ko: 이 카페에서는 한강 야경을 만끽할 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this cafe, you can fully enjoy the night view of the Han River.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날의 분위기를 만끽하며 커피를 마셨어요.
examples.en: I drank coffee, soaking in the mood of the rainy day.

explain: '즐기다'보다 기분이나 분위기를 가득 충분히 느낀다는 느낌이 강해요. 자유, 여유, 휴가, 봄, 해방감처럼 느끼는 대상을 목적어로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 일상의 활동에는 '즐기다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '즐기다' (to enjoy), like soaking up a feeling or atmosphere to the full. It is often used with things you feel, such as freedom, leisure, vacation, spring and a sense of release. For everyday activities, '즐기다' sounds more natural.

examples.en: When the show ended, the audience gave it a big round of applause.
Applause burst out after the speech ended.
He stepped down from the stage amid applause.
The rookie singer received great applause.
Applause poured in for the young performer.
I was moved by the applause and started to cry.

explain: 그냥 '박수'보다 크고 칭찬이 담긴 환호의 느낌이에요. '받다, 보내다, 쏟아지다, 터져 나오다'와 함께 써요. 말할 때는 '박수를 많이 받았어요'처럼 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It feels bigger than plain '박수', with cheering and praise. It pairs with verbs like 받다, 보내다, 쏟아지다 and 터져 나오다. In casual speech people often just say '박수를 많이 받았어요'.

en: fight valiantly; put up a strong fight

examples.en: Our players fought hard until the very end.
The team put up a strong fight but sadly lost.

examples.ko: 약한 팀이 강팀을 상대로 분전하고 있어요.
examples.en: The weaker team is putting up a strong fight against the strong team.
Applause poured out for the player who fought to the end.
Everyone gave their all, and we barely managed a draw.
The way they fought hard looked really cool.

explain: '열심히 하다'와 비슷하지만, 분전하다는 힘든 상대나 어려운 상황에서 온 힘을 다해 맞선다는 느낌이 있어요. 스포츠 뉴스에서 '아쉽게 졌지만 분전했다'처럼 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '열심히 했어요'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is like '열심히 하다', but '분전하다' carries the feeling of facing a tough opponent or situation with all one's strength. In sports news you often see '아쉽게 졌지만 분전했다'. In daily talk people say '열심히 했어요' more.

examples.en: I went to a dog cafe and played with the puppies.

examples.ko: 저는 애견 미용실에 한 달에 한 번 가요.
examples.en: I go to the dog grooming salon once a month.
Many people walk with their dogs.
A dog-only playground opened in the park.
My dog was sick, so I took it to the vet.
Dog food is cheaper online than at the supermarket.

explain: '강아지'나 '개'는 평소 쓰는 말이고, 애견은 사랑하는 개라는 느낌이 있어요. 하지만 '애견 카페', '애견 용품'처럼 가게나 물건 이름에 가장 자주 나와요. 고양이는 '애묘'라고 해요.
explain_en: 강아지 and 개 are everyday words, while 애견 carries the feeling of a loved dog. It most often appears in shop and product names such as 애견 카페 and 애견 용품. For cats the matching word is 애묘.

examples.ko: 심판의 판정에 관중이 일제히 야유를 보냈어요.
examples.en: The crowd all booed the referee's call at once.

examples.ko: 선수가 실수하자 여기저기서 야유가 터져 나왔어요.
examples.en: When the player made a mistake, boos broke out all around.

examples.ko: 야유 속에서도 그는 끝까지 노래를 불렀어요.
examples.en: Even amid the jeering, he sang to the end.

examples.ko: 공연 중에 야유를 받아서 가수가 많이 속상해했대요.
examples.en: I heard the singer was very upset after being booed during the show.

examples.ko: 박수는 못 칠망정 야유는 하지 말아야죠.
examples.en: Even if you can't clap, you shouldn't boo.

examples.ko: 의원의 연설 도중 야유 때문에 회의장이 소란스러웠어요.
examples.en: The hall was noisy because of the jeering during the lawmaker's speech.

explain: '야유를 보내다', '야유를 받다', '야유를 퍼붓다'처럼 자주 써요. 반대로 '박수'나 '환호'와 짝으로 떠올리면 쉬워요. '야유회'는 한자가 달라서 이 말과 관계가 없어요.
explain_en: It is often used as '야유를 보내다' (to boo), '야유를 받다' (to be booed) and '야유를 퍼붓다' (to hurl jeers). It is easy to remember as the opposite of '박수' (applause) or '환호' (cheers). '야유회' (company outing) uses different Chinese characters and is unrelated.

examples.en: Our team won a complete victory in the final.
Today's game was a total win from start to finish.
We expected an easy win, but it was unexpectedly close.
We started the tournament with a clean win, so the mood is good.

examples.ko: 상대가 약해서 완승이 쉬울 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: I thought a total win would be easy because the opponent was weak.
A complete win in the very first game of the season, that's amazing.

explain: '완승을 거두다'로 자주 쓰고 반의어는 '완패'예요. 스포츠뿐 아니라 선거에서도 쓰며, '압승'은 큰 차이로 이긴다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It commonly appears as '완승을 거두다', and its opposite is '완패'. It is used in elections as well as sports, and '압승' puts more stress on winning by a big margin.

examples.ko: 외래문화를 받아들이면서 우리 생활도 많이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: As we accepted foreign culture, our daily life changed a lot too.
Young people have little resistance to foreign culture.
Halloween is a foreign culture to us, but it has become familiar now.
It's a street where foreign culture and traditional culture blend together.

examples.ko: 외래문화만 무조건 따라 하는 건 좋지 않다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think it's not good to blindly copy only foreign culture.

examples.ko: 이 수업에서는 외래문화가 언어에 준 영향을 배워요.
examples.en: In this class we learn about the influence foreign culture had on language.

explain: '전통문화', '토착문화'와 짝으로 생각하면 쉬워요. '외래'는 '외래어', '외래종'처럼 밖에서 들어온 것 앞에 붙어요. 문장에 따라 '전통을 위협한다'는 분위기가 될 수도 있어요.
explain_en: It is easy to think of it as a pair with '전통문화' or '토착문화'. '외래' goes before things that came in from outside, as in '외래어' and '외래종'. Depending on the sentence, it can carry a tone of 'threatening tradition'.

examples.en: The players smiled brightly, holding the trophy.
The team name is engraved on the trophy.
The trophy is on display at the museum.

examples.ko: 이번 대회 우승컵의 주인은 우리 학교예요.
examples.en: The owner of this tournament's trophy is our school.
Only one game is left before the trophy.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 3년 만에 우승컵 하나를 가져왔어요.
examples.en: That team brought home a trophy for the first time in three years.

explain: '트로피'도 같은 물건을 말하지만 우승컵은 컵 모양일 때 더 자연스러워요. 상으로 받는 '메달'이나 '상장'은 따로 불러요. '우승컵을 들어 올리다', '우승컵을 차지하다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: 트로피 can name the same object, but 우승컵 is more natural when it is cup-shaped. A 메달 or a 상장 given as a prize has its own name. It is often used as 우승컵을 들어 올리다 or 우승컵을 차지하다.

examples.en: The marathon winner put a laurel wreath on his head.
The athlete smiled brightly wearing the laurel wreath.

examples.ko: 올림픽에서 월계관의 주인공이 되는 게 목표예요.
examples.en: My goal is to be the one who wins the laurel wreath at the Olympics.
I heard that in ancient Greece the laurel wreath was a symbol of victory.

examples.ko: 월계관 없이 돌아왔지만 모두가 박수를 쳐 줬어요.
examples.en: He came back without the laurel wreath, but everyone applauded him.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에서 월계관은 우리 팀에게 돌아갔어요.
examples.en: At this tournament, the laurel wreath went to our team.

explain: 우승과 승리, 영광을 상징해서 대회 우승 이야기에서 멋있게 표현할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 보통 '우승하다'라고 말하고, '월계관을 쓰다/차지하다'는 기사나 이야기 속 표현으로 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It stands for victory and glory, and is used to describe winning a tournament in a stylish way. In everyday talk people usually just say '우승하다', while '월계관을 쓰다/차지하다' fits news articles and storytelling.

examples.ko: 동생이 미술 대회에서 입상해서 가족이 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling placed in an art contest and the whole family was happy.

examples.ko: 이번 공모전에서 입상하면 상금을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you place in this contest, you can receive prize money.
Even though I didn't win a prize, it was a good experience.
Our team placed at the national competition!

examples.ko: 입상한 작품은 다음 달에 시청에서 전시해요.
examples.en: The prize-winning works will be displayed at city hall next month.
How much do I have to practice to win a prize?

explain: '상을 받다'와 달리 '입상하다'는 대회나 공모전에서 순위 안에 들어 상을 받을 때 써요. 정확한 등수는 '1등을 하다'처럼 따로 말해요. '입상자', '입상작'도 같이 알아 두세요.
explain_en: Unlike a general '상을 받다', '입상하다' is used when you place within the ranking in a contest or competition and receive a prize. The exact rank is said separately, as in '1등을 하다'. Also learn '입상자' (prize winner) and '입상작' (prize-winning work).

examples.ko: 두 팀이 우승을 놓고 쟁탈전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two teams fought a fierce battle for the title.

examples.ko: 인기 상품이라 사려는 사람들 사이에 쟁탈전이 일어났어요.
examples.en: It was a popular item, so a scramble broke out among buyers.
Booking holiday train tickets is a scramble every time.
Many teams have jumped into this contest.
The living room was noisy because of the fight over the remote.
The scramble finally ended with rock-paper-scissors.

explain: '경쟁'보다 한정된 자리나 물건을 서로 차지하려고 다툰다는 느낌이 강해요. 우승, 자리, 인기 상품 이야기에 많이 쓰고, '리모컨 쟁탈전'처럼 장난스럽게도 말해요. '쟁탈전을 벌이다/펼치다'가 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
explain_en: Compared with '경쟁', it feels more like people fighting to grab a limited seat or item. It is used for titles, seats and popular goods, and playfully as in '리모컨 쟁탈전'. '쟁탈전을 벌이다/펼치다' are natural partners.

examples.en: Our team advanced to the semifinal.

examples.ko: 준결승은 내일 저녁 일곱 시에 시작해요.
examples.en: The semifinal starts at seven tomorrow evening.
We lost the semifinal by a narrow margin.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 준결승까지 한 골도 내주지 않았어요.
examples.en: That player hadn't conceded a single goal until the semifinal.

examples.ko: 준결승 경기를 보러 친구와 경기장에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the stadium with a friend to watch the semifinal match.
If we win the semifinal, we meet in the final.

explain: 순서는 '예선, 8강, 4강(준결승), 결승'이에요. 스포츠 뉴스에서는 준결승보다 '4강'이라는 말을 더 자주 써요. 준결승에서 진 팀끼리 '3·4위전'을 해요.
explain_en: The order is 예선, 8강, 4강 (준결승), 결승. In sports news 4강 is often used instead of 준결승. The two teams that lose the semifinals play a 3·4위전.

examples.en: Our team suffered a crushing defeat in the final.

examples.ko: 축구 대회에서 우리 학교가 참패했다는 소식을 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard the news that our school was crushed in the soccer tournament.
Even after the crushing defeat, the players greeted the fans with a smile to the end.
This crushing defeat happened because we were not prepared enough.
After the crushing defeat, the coach apologized to the fans.
The fans were very disappointed by the string of crushing defeats.

explain: '완패'가 완전히 졌다는 뜻이라면 '참패'는 처참할 만큼 크게 졌다는 느낌이 더 강해요. 반대말은 '대승'이고 '참패를 당하다', '참패하다'로 많이 써요. 스포츠, 선거, 시험 결과 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '완패' means losing completely, while '참패' adds a stronger sense of a devastating, humiliating loss. The opposite is '대승' (big win), and it is often used as '참패를 당하다' or '참패하다'. It appears often in news about sports, elections and results.

examples.en: The city founded a new soccer team.

examples.ko: 동네 사람들이 모여서 합창단을 창단하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Neighbors got together and decided to start a choir.
The school is founding a baseball club for the first time this year.
That coach is the person who founded the team.
To start an orchestra, you first need members.

examples.ko: 저는 대학 때 밴드를 창단할 생각이었어요.
examples.en: In college I was planning to form a band.

explain: 팀이나 합창단, 악단처럼 '단'이 붙는 단체를 처음 만들 때 써요. 회사를 만들 때는 '설립하다'나 '세우다'라고 해요. 팀이 처음 생기는 일은 주로 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is used when you start a group ending in 단, such as a team, choir, or orchestra. For a company, say 설립하다 or 세우다. You hear it most often in sports news about new teams.

examples.en: My daughter won a prize at a piano competition.

examples.ko: 이번 콩쿠르에는 전 세계에서 젊은 연주자들이 참가했어요.
examples.en: Young performers from all over the world took part in this competition.

examples.ko: 콩쿠르를 준비하느라 매일 여섯 시간씩 연습해요.
examples.en: I practice six hours a day to prepare for the competition.

examples.ko: 국제 콩쿠르 우승은 연주자에게 큰 기회예요.
examples.en: Winning an international competition is a big opportunity for a performer.

examples.ko: 다음 달 콩쿠르가 끝나면 같이 여행 가요.
examples.en: Let's go on a trip together after next month's competition ends.

examples.ko: 콩쿠르 심사 위원들 앞에서 연주하니까 많이 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was very nervous playing in front of the competition judges.

explain: 음악이나 무용 같은 예술 분야의 경연 대회에 주로 써요. 프랑스어 concours에서 온 말이에요. 노래나 말하기 같은 일반 대회는 '대회'나 '경연 대회'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is mainly used for competitions in the arts, such as music or dance, and comes from the French word concours. General contests like singing or speech events are called '대회' or '경연 대회'.

examples.en: The national team's warm-up match is held before the World Cup.
Our team won 2-1 in today's warm-up match.

examples.ko: 감독은 평가전을 통해 선수들의 상태를 확인했어요.
examples.en: The coach checked the players' condition through the warm-up match.

examples.ko: 주말에 평가전을 보러 경기장에 갈 거예요.
examples.en: I'm going to the stadium to watch the warm-up match this weekend.
The warm-up results were good, so my expectations are high.
The warm-up match was canceled because of rain.

explain: '평가전'은 큰 대회 전에 실력과 전술을 시험해 보는 경기예요. 순위에 영향이 큰 '본선'이나 '정규 경기'와 달라서 결과보다 준비 과정이 중요해요. 축구, 야구 같은 스포츠 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: A 평가전 is a match played before a major tournament to test form and tactics. Unlike a 본선 or a regular league match, the result matters less than the preparation. It appears often in sports news for soccer and baseball.

examples.en: I saw a huge pyramid in Egypt.
I'm still curious how the pyramids were built.
I want to climb to the top of the pyramid.

examples.ko: 아이들이 컵을 쌓아 피라미드 모양을 만들었어요.
examples.en: The kids stacked cups into a pyramid shape.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 피라미드 구조라서 위에 있는 사람이 적어요.
examples.en: This company has a pyramid structure, so few people are at the top.
Many tourists take photos at the pyramids.

explain: 피라미드는 이집트 유적 말고도 '인구 피라미드', '피라미드 구조'처럼 아래가 넓고 위가 좁은 모양을 빗대어 써요. 또 불법 다단계 사업을 줄여서 '피라미드'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: Besides the Egyptian monuments, 피라미드 is used figuratively for anything wide at the bottom and narrow at the top, as in 인구 피라미드 and 피라미드 구조. People also shorten an illegal multi-level scheme to just 피라미드.

examples.ko: 어제 우리 팀 선발투수가 호투를 펼쳤어요.
examples.en: Our team's starting pitcher pitched very well yesterday.
Thanks to the great pitching, the team won 3 to 1.

examples.ko: 신인 투수의 호투가 팬들을 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: The rookie pitcher's strong performance surprised the fans.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 시즌 초반 호투로 주목받았어요.
examples.en: That player drew attention with his good pitching early in the season.
Despite the great pitching, the team ended up losing.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기의 호투 장면을 다시 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched the great pitching moments from today's game again.

explain: 야구에서 투수가 잘 던지는 것을 말하고, 기사 제목에도 자주 나와요. '호투를 펼치다'가 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 반대로 못 던질 때는 '부진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes a pitcher throwing well in baseball and often appears in article headlines. '호투를 펼치다' is a common pairing. When a pitcher does poorly, people say '부진'.
